data.traefik:
# Traefik reference config for kimai, generated by the hub from its image.yml.
# Labels for the kimai service in your compose file. Traefik's docker provider must reach the kimai
# container on a shared network; the entrypoint websecure and the certificate resolver letsencrypt are
# examples from a typical Traefik setup. Replace example.com with your domain. Websockets need nothing extra.
services:
  kimai:
    labels:
      - traefik.enable=true
      - traefik.http.services.kimai.loadbalancer.server.port=80
      - traefik.http.routers.kimai.rule=Host(`kimai.example.com`)
      - traefik.http.routers.kimai.entrypoints=websecure
      - traefik.http.routers.kimai.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt
      - traefik.http.routers.kimai.service=kimai
      # Authentication: uncomment one; the middleware is defined in your Traefik config.
      # - traefik.http.routers.kimai.middlewares=authelia@docker
      # - traefik.http.routers.kimai.middlewares=authentik@docker
      # API paths stay open so client applications keep working.
      - traefik.http.routers.kimai-api.rule=Host(`kimai.example.com`) && (PathPrefix(`/api`))
      - traefik.http.routers.kimai-api.entrypoints=websecure
      - traefik.http.routers.kimai-api.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt
      - traefik.http.routers.kimai-api.service=kimai
      - traefik.http.routers.kimai-api.priority=100
